report:
PASS for the exact retained partial result, including its expressly conditional envelope conclusions. This does not solve original P13.1. I checked the author argument, all four canonical notes and the relevant supplied proof bodies, and opened all five matching primary PDFs. Env is an antecedent of the envelope theorem, not an established external premise.

For n1, the Gauss construction works with semivaluation supports. Among homogeneous components of least translated value, choose an extreme character using an additive total order. In a product, its extreme contribution is unique among the least-value contributions; higher-value contributions cannot cancel it. This establishes multiplicativity even when some values are infinite. Torification has the homogeneous support ideal consisting of elements whose every component has infinite value. On invariant points, translation preserves that support. Finite minima establish continuity, and translation by the opposite parameter supplies the inverse. These maps are a group action on the invariant locus; on arbitrary points, the zero-parameter Gauss construction is torification.

The slice argument is valid. At least one homogeneous generator has finite value at every punctured point. The minimum of the translated generator values is continuous, strictly increasing and has opposite infinite endpoint limits. Its unique zero occurs at rho_eta(v). At that translate, all generator values are nonnegative and one is zero, which establishes membership in S. On S, nonnegativity extends to all of R. The homogeneous-polynomial argument proves the claimed generator-independent reference potential. The carrier is compact and closed, and torification retracts the full link onto it.

Every occurring nonzero weight is a nonnegative integral combination of generator weights. Consequently its degree ratio is a weighted average of generator ratios. This proves the l,u bounds and the compact-Reeb Lipschitz bound for delta without rationality or denominator restrictions. The nonnegative valuative T comparison follows directly from the same denominator inequalities.

The slope inequalities establish the full finite/minus-infinite orbit dichotomy. At finite points, the orbit function is Lipschitz, strictly decreasing and surjective onto R. The root formula therefore exists uniquely and agrees exactly with the transported FS presentation. Presentation independence follows from this intrinsic definition. For CPSH approximation, the compact set actually needed is the image of A times a bounded root interval under translation; it is compact and stays punctured. Uniform error epsilon there gives root error at most epsilon/l. Compact torifications handle arbitrary full-cone compact sets. For decreasing nets, the displayed finite-root estimate gives convergence at finite points, while the signed root sandwich forces convergence to minus infinity at the remaining points. The transported limit is nontrivial. Zero sets and finite-value loci then establish inverse, cocycle and order identities, including singular orbits.

The trivial-semivaluation normalization and fixed-measure bounds are correct. Nontriviality forces a finite value at the trivial point. For nonpositive potentials, the inequalities have the displayed directions, including extended values; ordinary domination proves the fixed-probability L1 statement. The constant-shift counterexample is correct. C itself does not descend through the raw equivalence relation modulo constants. Choosing the unique representative phi-phi(v_triv) does induce a bijection of quotient sets, with inverse and cocycle inherited from normalized transport. This is neither additive nor an energy identification.

The density result is confined correctly to S. The valuations ord_(x-y) and v_triv provide the asserted full-link counterexample. On S, a homogeneous function distinguishes distinct invariant points, and its bounded truncation supplies a difference of genuine FS functions separating them. The real lattice identity is valid. One routine approximation step should be explicit: common-degree products first prove the sum assertion for rational degree/coefficient ratios; arbitrary real coefficients follow by uniform approximation and CPSH closedness. Rational approximation of the Reeb field followed by root transport supplies the irrational passage. Thus the lattice Stone–Weierstrass application establishes density in C(S).

For n2, A_eta(m) is the integral of the nonnegative filtration dimensions, so it is monotone under the cumulative graded-space inclusions. This is precisely where nonnegative jumps matter. Uniform linear boundedness gives bounded rescaled jump support, allowing the source weak limit to determine first moments. Floor/ceiling sandwiches establish real-cutoff limits for both N and A. Taking asymptotics and dividing positive volumes gives l^n/u^(n+1) and u^n/l^(n+1), hence the exponent 2n+1. The zero-S case and the growth-threshold comparison require no logarithm or finite generation of the filtration. The printed finite equalities between A/(mN) and n!A/(vol m^(n+1)) are only asymptotic; the retained proof uses the correct jumping-average limit.

The degree-filtration diagnostic is exact: chi(x)=chi(y)=1 induces rho+1, whose probability-normalized energy is 1, whereas A/(mN)=2/3 for every positive integer m. It genuinely contradicts the printed E=S identity with those definitions. No corrected general energy identity is needed or imported. For the same-Reeb energy comparison, consecutive mixed integrals differ by the negative Hodge pairing, so they decrease from the psi endpoint to the phi endpoint. Their average gives the retained concavity inequalities. The repaired mixed-integral estimate also checks: writing B=max_i(-E(phi_i)), positivity and concavity give integral(tau MA(tau)) >= -nB; the mixed expansion and phi_0<=0 give the upper bound with coefficient (n-1)!/n^n. Combining them gives exactly the stated constant n^(n+1)/(n-1)!. There are n-1 potential factors, one radial link factor, volume normalization and energy denominator n vol throughout. For n=1 the empty-product case is direct; the Hodge argument is needed only for n>=2.

For n3, Proj R is projective after a suitable Veronese, and its affine degree-zero charts are normal by the supplied integral-closure argument. Over the stipulated field it is geometrically normal and geometrically unibranch. Passing to d gives an honest ample L_d, and the polarization is exactly L_d/(sd). Raising each FS section of integral degree e_j to degree D produces coefficient 1/(sD), confirming that factor. No quotient-singularity hypothesis is needed. A residual-torus linearization can be obtained by twisting the T-linearization by a character whose restriction cancels the subgroup's fibre weight; this choice does not change the trivial-valued metric. The larger G_m carrier and smaller fixed T carrier are distinct and are correctly related by residual torification. In dimension one, effectiveness leaves no nonproportional Reeb pair.

Under Env, the lifted continuous obstacle has a continuous invariant projective psh envelope. The torus supremum of an FS approximation is the finite maximum of its weight components: avoiding zeros of the leading residue Laurent polynomial proves the lower bound, including at points with support. The empty common zero locus remains empty, and the approximation error is unchanged. Hence the envelope descends to genuine cone CPSH. Conversely, cone CPSH approximants correspond to projective continuous psh metrics, and their nontrivial decreasing limit is projective psh. The projective net and sequence conventions agree through the checked regularization results. This proves both competitor directions.

The bounded-obstacle estimates and irrational passage are correct. Truncating competitors into [-M,0], transporting and subtracting kappa M gives the 2kappa M comparison; comparison with the transported rational envelope gives 3kappa M. There is a harmless scope clarification: the latter estimate uses the centered obstacle imposed at the start of Section 8. For arbitrary h, with c=sup h, its correct form is ||C_(zeta,xi)(P_zeta(h-c))+c-P_xi h|| <= 3kappa osc(h). An uncentered transport estimate would be false for constant obstacles. The first envelope estimate holds for arbitrary h because fixed-Reeb envelopes commute with constants. Rational approximation has delta tending to zero, and fixed-xi equivariance converts uniform carrier convergence into actual local-uniform convergence. The decreasing-obstacle argument is valid under its stated psh-envelope and nontrivial-limiting-competitor hypotheses.

The new source's theorem scope and dependency route are represented correctly. Its countability restriction cannot be dropped for a trivially valued field without the separate descent argument. APW imports, the reference reduction and the unrestricted-field compatibility steps are retained inside Env. The PL competitor restriction and contact-support inclusion are necessary source corrections. A further harmless source typo in Lemma 6.6 is that the strict supporting inequality needs l(t'), rather than l(t). None of these observations establishes Env. The conditional transfer needs its projective envelope consequence and does not purport to validate the preprint's missing proof dependencies. [Lyuhui Wu v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.27610v1).

For n4, the cited differentiability results remain correctly restricted to their own settings. Fixed-Reeb finite-energy continuity does not authorize changing-Reeb limits. The projective derivative theorem uses an existing energy extension and positive mixed intersection masses; the synthetic theorem requires additive ordered forms and its orthogonality/submean hypotheses. These structures are not supplied by root transport. No E1 preservation, moving-measure tail bound, cone orthogonality, energy extension, uniform derivative or P13.2 existence conclusion is inferred. Hashes, finite diagnostics and TeX claims are documentary evidence only and were not used to establish the mathematical verdict.

passages.statement: For a fixed Reeb field eta on a normal polarized affine cone of dimension n>=1 over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, the genuine positive mixed current of n-1 CPSH(eta) potentials and d'd''max(rho_eta,0), divided by vol(eta), is a Radon probability measure on X0. Its construction is symmetric and multilinear and extends by local-uniform psh approximation. For FS potentials its support is contained in X0^T. Wu24, Definition-Proposition 3.7 and Proposition 4.2(1); Wu22, Corollary 5.7.
passages.quote: a Radon probability measure supported on X0

passages.statement: For a fixed Reeb field eta on a normal polarized affine cone of dimension n>=1 over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, the genuine positive mixed current of n-1 CPSH(eta) potentials and d'd''max(rho_eta,0), divided by vol(eta), is a Radon probability measure on X0. Its construction is symmetric and multilinear and extends by local-uniform psh approximation. For FS potentials its support is contained in X0^T. Wu24, Definition-Proposition 3.7 and Proposition 4.2(1); Wu22, Corollary 5.7.

In the same fixed-Reeb setting with n>=2, let u and v be real multiples of differences of CPSH(eta) potentials, and let psi_1,...,psi_(n-2) belong to CPSH(eta). With Theta=d'd''psi_1 wedge ... wedge d'd''psi_(n-2) wedge d'd''max(rho_eta,0), integration by parts gives integral(u d'd''v wedge Theta)=integral(v d'd''u wedge Theta), and the Hodge inequality gives integral(u d'd''u wedge Theta)<=0. Wu24, Propositions 3.8–3.9, on this common-polarization difference domain.

In the same fixed-Reeb setting with n>=2, let u and v be real multiples of differences of CPSH(eta) potentials, and let psi_1,...,psi_(n-2) belong to CPSH(eta). With Theta=d'd''psi_1 wedge ... wedge d'd''psi_(n-2) wedge d'd''max(rho_eta,0), integration by parts gives integral(u d'd''v wedge Theta)=integral(v d'd''u wedge Theta), and the Hodge inequality gives integral(u d'd''u wedge Theta)<=0. Wu24, Propositions 3.8–3.9, on this common-polarization difference domain.

For a fixed Reeb field eta in the stipulated affine-cone setting, a decreasing net of actual PSH(eta) functions has a pointwise limit that either belongs to PSH(eta) or is identically minus infinite. Wu24, Proposition 5.2(3).

For a normal polarized affine cone and a decreasing, left-continuous, multiplicative, T-invariant filtration F with F^0R=R, exhaustive finite restrictions on each weight space and finite linear-growth threshold, the nonnegative cumulative jumping average A_eta(m)/(m dim R_eta(m)) converges to a finite S_eta for every Reeb field eta, including irrational fields. Also n! dim R_eta(m)/m^n converges to the positive cone volume vol(eta). Wu22, Theorem 3.3, Theorem 3.12 and Corollary 3.13.

For a normal positively graded affine cone of dimension n>=2 with primitive integral Reeb field eta_0, V=Proj R and its ample rational polarization L_0, V^an identifies homeomorphically with the G_m(eta_0)-invariant zero slice of the reference potential. Common-degree homogeneous FS lists identify with global FS metrics on L_0, with the reference potential corresponding to the trivial metric. Under this identification the projective mixed current of n-1 corresponding metrics pushes forward to the cone mixed current with its radial link factor. Wu22, Lemmas 5.11–5.12 and Proposition 5.13, retaining the rational line-bundle and stabilizer data.
passages.quote: the maps are inverses to each other

passages.statement: On a projective variety over a trivially valued field, at a fixed ample rational polarization, a generically finite decreasing net of projective psh functions has a projective psh limit; continuous psh functions are uniform limits of global FS functions at that polarization. Projective psh functions admit decreasing regularization, and the regularization can be chosen as a sequence. Boucksom–Jonsson 1801.08229v4, Theorems 4.5 and 4.15, Corollary 4.16, Example 3.9 and Corollary 12.18.

For one fixed Reeb field xi, 0<=p<=n-1, phi_1,...,phi_p in E^1(xi), and the remaining n-1-p potentials in FS(xi), Wu24 Theorem 6.3 constructs a unique normalized mixed Radon probability measure supported on X0. Every E^1(xi) testing potential is integrable against it after subtracting the reference, and the resulting pairing is continuous along decreasing nets whose testing and varying potential limits remain in E^1(xi).

For one projective variety over a trivially valued field, one fixed ample class omega and f in PL(X)_R, Boucksom–Jonsson 1801.08229v4 Theorem 8.5 gives E_omega^down(phi+epsilon f)=E_omega(phi)+epsilon integral(f MA_omega(phi))+O(epsilon^2) for every phi in E^1(omega), with the remainder constant uniform in phi. The extension E^down is the extension defined in Section 8; identification with E composed with the envelope additionally has the hypotheses stated there.

Boucksom–Jonsson 2307.01697v1 uses a common compact Hausdorff space, a dense real test vector space containing constants, an additively ordered vector space of closed forms whose positive cone spans it and is closed in the finest vector-space topology, a linear ddc vanishing on constants, and nonzero symmetric positive mixed measure products satisfying integration by parts and Hodge negativity. Section 4 additionally assumes the orthogonality and submean properties of Definitions 2.15 and 1.26. For omega>=0 with positive class and a finite-energy probability measure mu, Theorem 4.8 then gives d/dt at t=0 of J_(omega+t theta)(mu)=J_omega^theta(mu) for theta in the form space, using the reference extension of Remark 2.4 when omega+t theta need not remain positive.
